description: We are a team of BS Information Technology students bringing data to life by telling engaging stories through code, data, and design.
summary:
Project Remember Me: The Untold Story of the Forgotten is a web-based, game-like interactive storytelling experience that brings the forgotten stories of space equipment on the Moon and Mars to life. Players take on the role of Space Commanders, travel between celestial bodies, complete exploration missions, and discover historical machines through interactive 3D models and first-person storytelling.

We address the lack of engagement among younger learners in science, particularly in space exploration, by turning space history into an experience that children and teens can actively participate in. Instead of simply reading facts or looking at pictures, they get to explore different environments, search for equipment, complete missions, and unlock stories as they progress through the game. This makes learning more interactive and gives them a reason to stay curious and involved.

Beyond making science more engaging, the project also aims to preserve an important part of space history. By sharing the stories, purposes, and contributions of these machines, we hope to ensure that their role in humanity's exploration of space continues to be recognized and remembered.
details:
Project Remember Me: The Untold Story of the Forgotten is an interactive web-based experience built around a storytelling challenge, using a gaming approach to make learning much more engaging and fun. It works as a futuristic terminal where users act as "Space Commanders" who use a digital radar and orbital tools to scan planets, find lost space equipment, and learn their stories to remember.

The main benefit of this project is that it replaces passive reading with active exploration, helping students build a real emotional connection and curiosity toward the machines that made space travel possible.

The intended impact of the project is to greatly boost student interest, emotional engagement, and learning motivation while remaining very easy for anyone to use directly in a web browser on mobile or desktop without needing to log in.

To develop the project, the team used a variety of tools, coding languages, software, and hardware. They used Blender 5.1 to create custom 3D models, and HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and Three.js for frontend rendering and interactive parts. For coding and teamwork, they used VS Code, Git, GitHub, and Node.js. They also used ElevenLabs for system voiceovers, official NASA data and textures for scientific accuracy, and Claude to help write code and create visual effects.

The project is creative because it uses personified storytelling, allowing abandoned space machines to share their own historical journeys in the first person rather than presenting dry facts.

When building it, the team carefully considered factors like ease of use, deep user immersion, and strict scientific accuracy by basing everything on real NASA data and proven educational research on gamified learning.
